title: NbO2 Mott tripwire integrates row activations, fires neighbor refresh
idea: Effect: Mott insulator-metal transition. Each wordline strap gets a tiny RC node that receives a fixed charge packet per activation and leaks with a ~64 ms time constant; an NbO2 threshold switch (Mott transition ~800 C, so stable at 95 C, unlike VO2) across the node snaps metallic once the node crosses ~0.6 V (about N activations within the window) and pulses a refresh-request line for the two neighboring rows. The result is an analog, self-decaying per-row counter of ~100 nm^2 with no SRAM tracker tables.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): deterministic per-row detection at ~1k-activation thresholds, immune to many-sided tracker-evasion patterns; replaces CAM/SRAM trackers in the periphery (~5-10x less mitigation area) and removes probabilistic over-refresh.

title: Oersted-pushed magnetic domain wall counts activations per row
idea: Effect: field-driven domain-wall motion. A short perpendicular-magnetized CoFeB nanowire with ~64 pinning notches runs alongside each wordline driver; each activation current pulse's Oersted field advances a domain wall one notch, and when the wall reaches the last notch a small MTJ senses it, requests neighbor refresh and a reverse pulse rewinds the wall. The count is exact and non-volatile, and it is built in BEOL over the driver.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): exact per-row activation counts with zero SRAM area and no loss at power-down or self-refresh entry; avoids the 10-20% bandwidth cost of conservative probabilistic mitigations.

title: Thin-oxide tunneling canary cells set each row's refresh interval
idea: Effect: direct/Fowler-Nordheim tunneling plus subthreshold leakage, made deliberately stronger. Each row carries 2-4 canary cells whose access device has a thinner gate oxide and shorter channel, so they fail ~4x earlier than the weakest real cell with the same temperature and voltage dependence. Rows refresh at a long default interval (256 ms+) and drop to a shorter interval only when a periodic check finds a flipped canary.
why: Retention tail (fact 3): ~99% of rows run 4x longer refresh, cutting refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit) and the 10-20% bandwidth tax ~3-4x; the canaries track temperature and aging automatically, so no profiling database is needed.

title: Pyroelectric film senses heating transients and gates refresh rate
idea: Effect: pyroelectricity. A Sc-doped AlN patch per bank (CMOS-compatible and pyroelectric) outputs current proportional to dT/dt, giving a zero-bias, microsecond heating-event detector; refresh steps up only during and after thermal ramps (for example a GPU power spike), and banks sit at the slow rate while temperature is steady and cool.
why: Refresh is 16-33% of idle power (fact 3): today's slow polled thermal sensors force ~10 C guard bands and a blanket 2x refresh above 85 C; transient-aware refresh removes the guard band, giving ~2x longer average refresh intervals.

title: AlScN piezo patches strain leaky mats to raise access Vt
idea: Effect: piezoelectric actuation plus deformation-potential band shift. AlScN piezo patches deposited over each mat are biased after retention test so that mats with leakage tails get uniaxial stress on their buried-channel access transistors, shifting band edges and Vt by ~20-40 mV and reducing junction band-to-band tunneling. The bias can be retuned in the field as the part ages.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3) and yield: worst mats see ~2-3x less tail leakage, so tail-limited mats are used instead of spared out, and their refresh relaxes ~2x with no new cell-array masks.

title: Electrochromic contact images capacitor-dielectric defects across whole wafer
idea: Effect: electrochromism. After the capacitor dielectric step and before the top plate, a removable transparent electrolyte-plus-WO3 electrochromic contact is pressed onto the wafer and the bottom electrodes are biased through the substrate; cells whose dielectric leaks (pinholes, thin spots, pA-nA) color the film locally, and an optical scan maps millions of defect sites in seconds into a mat-level repair or rework map.
why: Capacitor leakage is a major retention-tail contributor (facts 1, 3): defects are caught at the step instead of after full flow and hours of multi-temperature retention test, raising yield and cutting test cost and scrap.

title: Ionization-current strike sentinels trigger instant local scrub
idea: Effect: radiation-induced photoconductivity in silicon. A sparse large-area reverse-biased junction sentinel per mat collects the ionization charge of an alpha or neutron strike as a current spike; the controller then immediately read-corrects-writes only the rows within the strike radius instead of waiting for a whole-device patrol scrub.
why: Soft errors and ECC strength: multi-bit accumulation within one codeword is caught within microseconds, so lighter on-die ECC (~6% instead of 12.5% parity) or lower-Qcrit (weaker, smaller) cells become acceptable.

title: Field-steered hydrogen re-passivates traps causing variable retention
idea: Effect: field- and heat-driven ion migration. For a mid-life self-heal, data is evacuated from a mat, built-in heater lines (wordlines driven in a heater mode) raise it to ~200 C for seconds, and a gate bias drifts mobile hydrogen from a SiN:H reservoir back to depassivated Si/SiO2 dangling bonds and GIDL-site traps that create variable-retention cells.
why: Retention-tail growth with age and hammer-induced interface damage: restores tails to near time-zero, so refresh intervals stay long and parts are healed instead of retired.

title: Phase-change thermal witness bits grade retired DRAM for second life
idea: Effect: thermal hysteresis (one-way amorphous-to-crystalline transitions). Each die holds a few chalcogenide witness cells of different compositions (Sb-rich, GeTe-rich, N-doped GST) that crystallize irreversibly after cumulative time above ~105/125/150 C, recording its thermal history. At datacenter decommission, a reader bins modules by witnessed stress plus a fast retention scan and resells them into edge, PC and CXL far-memory tiers at a derated refresh rate.
why: Usable supply: reclaims retired AI-server DDR/HBM on 3-5 year refresh cycles as trustworthy graded supply, maybe +10-20% effective bit supply with zero fab capex.

title: Telegraph-noise fingerprinting quarantines variable-retention cells
idea: Effect: random telegraph noise from single-trap capture and emission. A background test mode measures a suspected cell's retention repeatedly at several pause times; a VRT cell shows bimodal pass/fail statistics with characteristic dwell times, while a merely weak cell shows a single threshold. Only bimodal cells are remapped to a small per-bank spare-cell CAM.
why: VRT is why refresh cannot follow measured retention (fact 3): isolating the ~1e-6 VRT population makes profiled multi-rate refresh safe, cutting refresh operations ~70%.

title: Thin-film Peltier strips cool only refresh-dominant hot banks
idea: Effect: Peltier thermoelectric cooling. A Bi2Te3/Sb2Te3 superlattice thin-film cooler in the interposer under the HBM base die pumps heat out of the 2-4 banks sitting over GPU hotspots, dropping them ~10 C; the controller runs it only when the computed refresh-energy saving exceeds the Peltier power.
why: High-temperature refresh: leakage halves per ~10 C, so hot banks avoid the 2x refresh mode above 85 C, and the row-hammer threshold also improves at lower temperature.

title: Negative-capacitance ferroelectric gate steepens access-transistor turn-off
idea: Effect: ferroelectric negative capacitance. A thin Zr-doped HfO2 layer in the buried-wordline gate stack, capacitance-matched to the gate oxide, gives sub-60 mV/dec swing over the off region, so for the same on-current the tail off-leakage falls ~10x (or the wordline overdrive falls from ~3 V toward 2 V).
why: Leakage tail (fact 3) plus voltage floor (fact 10): ~4x+ retention, or ~30% lower wordline CV^2 energy.

title: Per-mat segmented back-bias wells tuned to measured leakage tail
idea: Effect: MOSFET body effect. The array p-well is split into per-mat wells isolated by deep n-well rings, each fed by a tiny local charge pump; mats with leakage tails get an extra -0.3 to -0.8 V reverse body bias (+60-100 mV Vt), while healthy mats stay at nominal bias and avoid the extra junction-field GIDL penalty.
why: Retention tail: ~5-10x leakage reduction on the worst mats without penalizing the whole die, so the refresh interval is set per mat, not by the die's worst cell.

title: Hot-carrier injection permanently nulls sense-amplifier offset
idea: Effect: hot-carrier injection and oxide charge trapping. At final test each bitline sense amplifier's offset is measured, and controlled high-drain-bias pulses on one transistor of the cross-coupled pair trap charge in its gate oxide, shifting its Vt to cancel the mismatch: a one-time analog trim with no extra transistors that cuts offset sigma from ~15 mV to ~3 mV.
why: Signal margin: the required cell signal scales with SA offset, so the same margin needs ~30-40% less Cs or tolerates more droop (longer retention); it also allows longer bitlines and fewer sense amps (periphery, fact 7).

title: Kirchhoff current-sum checksum scrubs rows inside the array
idea: Effect: Kirchhoff current summation. During refresh, the restored sense-amp outputs of each column group drive equal unit currents onto a shared analog sum line, so the total current encodes the group's Hamming weight; a comparator checks it against a weight value stored in spare cells at write time. Only rows whose weight changed are shipped to the ECC engine for correction.
why: Patrol scrub moves entire rows to the controller: in-array detection makes frequent scrubbing nearly free (~10x less scrub energy and zero channel bandwidth), so weaker-retention cells can be tolerated by scrubbing more often.

title: Negative wordline undershoot sweeps hammer-injected electrons back
idea: Effect: minority-carrier drift and recombination. Part of row hammer is electrons injected from the aggressor's inverted channel diffusing to the victim storage node; right after precharge, the aggressor wordline gets a ~2 ns negative undershoot that accumulates holes under the gate and recombines or drifts the injected electron cloud back before it reaches the victim. Only the wordline driver waveform changes.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): could raise HCfirst from ~1k toward 5-10k activations, shrinking tracker tables and mitigation refreshes ~5x.

title: Villari magnetostrictive sensors map TSV stress for zone-specific refresh
idea: Effect: inverse magnetostriction (Villari). FeGa thin-film stripes whose permeability changes with mechanical stress, read inductively, ring the TSV clusters in HBM core dies and report local stress during warpage and thermal cycling; the controller maps stress-induced (piezoresistive) leakage to zone-specific refresh rates instead of a die-wide guard band.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): measured stress lets designers narrow conservative TSV keep-out zones (recovering ~2-5% die area) and drops stress-driven refresh guard bands.

title: Deuterium anneal hardens access transistors against tail and hammer damage
idea: Effect: the giant isotope effect in Si-H/Si-D desorption. The final H2 forming anneal is replaced by a high-pressure D2 anneal; Si-D interface bonds are ~10-50x more resistant to hot-carrier and hammer-cycling desorption, so the interface-trap generation that grows VRT tails and hammer susceptibility over life slows sharply.
why: Lifetime reliability: keeps time-zero retention and hammer thresholds over years, so end-of-life guard bands shrink (~1.5-2x refresh relaxation). It is a drop-in process change.

title: Single-electron-transistor sense amp counts stored electrons directly
idea: Effect: Coulomb blockade. A single-electron transistor with a ~2 nm Si island (charging energy well above kT at room temperature) capacitively coupled to the bitline acts as a sub-electron electrometer; its periodic current oscillation (Coulomb staircase) resolves signals of a few hundred electrons, with reference cells calibrating background-charge drift.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): the Cs requirement could drop from ~5 fF to ~0.5 fF, and heavily drooped weak cells still read correctly, removing the AR-75 capacitor.

title: Spin-Hall SOT-MRAM parity layer sits atop the array in BEOL
idea: Effect: spin Hall effect (spin-orbit torque switching). A SOT-MRAM layer built in the BEOL above the cell array holds per-row ECC parity and error-history logs; spin-Hall writes avoid tunnel-barrier stress (high endurance), and parity reads proceed in parallel with the DRAM read.
why: On-die ECC costs ~6-12.5% of array area: moving parity off the silicon frees it (~10% density) and makes stronger codes affordable for weaker cells; the non-volatile error log survives power loss for predictive sparing.

title: Replica-node relaxation oscillator times refresh from real leakage
idea: Effect: Arrhenius thermally activated generation current. Each subarray has a replica storage node built from the same cell transistor and capacitor that discharges to a comparator threshold, resets and repeats; its frequency tracks that subarray's actual leakage versus temperature, voltage and aging, and it clocks the refresh counter with a fixed guard factor instead of a fixed 64 ms timer.
why: Removes fixed worst-case temperature guard bands: at typical 45-60 C operation, refresh rate falls ~4-8x versus 85 C worst-case timing.

title: Avalanche-gain gated diode preamplifies weak cell charge
idea: Effect: impact-ionization avalanche multiplication. A gated p-i-n diode at each sense node, biased just below breakdown and stabilized by a replica-diode bias loop, multiplies the small charge transferred from a weak cell ~10x (like an APD) before the latch sense amp resolves.
why: Makes 3-5x smaller signals readable, so leakier or smaller capacitors are acceptable, or bitlines can be longer with fewer sense amps (fact 7).

title: Resonant-tunneling diode pair makes each storage node self-restoring
idea: Effect: negative differential resistance in resonant tunneling. Each storage node is tied to a series pair of Si/SiGe RTDs stacked above the capacitor (a Goto pair), creating two stable node voltages; leakage only nudges the node and the NDR latch pulls it back, so data holds with no periodic refresh while a sub-pA standby current flows.
why: Retention tail and refresh (fact 3): refresh-free DRAM removes ~46 fJ/bit refresh energy and 10-20% bandwidth; 1e10 cells x 1 pA is only ~10 mA standby.

title: Electrocaloric heat-pump layer makes 0.3 fF stacked cells refresh-viable
idea: Effect: electrocaloric cooling. A 64-tier monolithic stack of thin-film cells with only ~0.3 fF planar MIM caps (no high-AR pillar) sits on a P(VDF-TrFE-CFE) or PST electrocaloric film; field cycling of the film pumps heat solid-state toward the sink, holding the stack ~20 K below its neighbors, which cuts thermal-generation leakage ~4-6x so 0.3 fF cells still retain ~16 ms.
why: 10x density: 64 tiers at ~0.2x per-tier density is ~13x bits/mm^2. Same cost: the 5-7 EUV layers and AR-75 capacitor etch are traded for repeated deposition, with the electrocaloric film as a cheap package layer.

title: Parametric charge pumping on common plate regenerates all cells continuously
idea: Effect: parametric amplification via a nonlinear C(V). Each storage node is a nonlinear MOS varactor plus a rectifying junction; a shared AC drive on the common plate pumps charge with a voltage-dependent sign, creating two stable fixed points, so every cell continuously restores itself toward its nearer rail with no row-by-row refresh. Reads compare node charge against a mid-level reference.
why: 10x density: cells tolerating ~1000x more leakage can be 2-terminal crosspoint varactor-diode stacks at 4F^2 in 8 BEOL layers (~10x); refresh counters, timers and restore-heavy sense periphery (fact 7) disappear, holding cost.

title: Latch resolution time becomes LDPC soft information for weak cells
idea: Effect: regenerative metastability, where a latch's resolution time grows as log(1/input). A time-to-digital tap shared across 8 sense amps records how fast each SA resolved, giving a per-bit confidence (LLR) to a soft-decision LDPC decoder over a 2 KB page, so raw BER ~1e-3 becomes acceptable versus ~1e-6 for SECDED.
why: 10x density: 1000x raw-BER tolerance lets ~0.5 fF thin-film Si cells stack 32 tiers at ~0.35x per-tier density (~11x bits/mm^2). Same cost: ~10% LDPC parity and decoders amortized across banks.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pool lets capacitorless gain cells hold for hours
idea: Effect: carrier freeze-out and suppressed thermal generation at 77 K. A CXL-attached rack memory pool runs at 77 K, where generation current falls >1e10x and kT noise drops 4x, so 2-transistor gain cells with only ~0.05-0.1 fF parasitic node capacitance hold data seconds to hours and their tiny signals read cleanly. There is no capacitor module and almost no refresh.
why: 10x density: capacitorless 2T cells stacked 16 tiers give ~10x bits/mm^2. Same cost: no capacitor module or EUV; the cryocooler (~10 W/W at 77 K) is amortized because a refresh-free pool dissipates little.

title: Dielectric-absorption reservoir backs up charge in tiny capacitors
idea: Effect: dielectric absorption (Debye relaxation, 'soakage'). The storage capacitor is a bilayer of thin fast high-k plus a slow polar layer with tau ~ms; on write the slow layer partially polarizes, and as leakage drains the fast charge, its relaxation current flows back into the node, stretching retention of a 0.5 fF cap several-fold. A two-step read (fast charge, then soaked charge) gives a second vote for marginal cells.
why: 10x density: 0.5 fF planar caps with ~3x retention extension stack 24 tiers at ~0.4x per-tier density (~10x). Same cost: the AR-75 pillar etch and its EUV patterning are removed.

title: Per-tier Seebeck thermopiles let 100-tier stacks refresh by tier
idea: Effect: Seebeck thermoelectric voltage. In a ~100-tier 3D DRAM whose inner tiers run 10-20 K hotter than outer ones, thermocouple pairs formed in the staircase contacts read each tier's temperature with zero bias power; the controller assigns per-tier refresh intervals (cool tiers ~4x longer) and steers hot data to cool tiers.
why: 10x density: without per-tier refresh the hottest tier sets refresh for all 100, a 30-40% bandwidth tax at 3D densities; keeping it under 10% makes a ~100-tier (~10x) stack viable, with thermocouples added to existing staircase steps at near-zero cost.

title: Quantum-confined 2 nm channels widen bandgap and kill generation leakage
idea: Effect: quantum confinement. Access transistors of stacked lateral cells are ~2 nm-thick Si nanosheets in a Si/SiGe superlattice stack; confinement raises the effective bandgap ~0.3-0.4 eV, and because generation leakage scales ~exp(-Eg/2kT), off-state tails fall ~100-1000x, so ~0.5 fF suffices for 64 ms.
why: 10x density: no AR-75 capacitor and a 40-tier epitaxial superlattice stack (3D-NAND-style staircase) gives ~10x bits/mm^2. Same cost: one deep-etch module and epi replace the EUV-heavy capacitor and cell layers.

title: Inline photoluminescence maps each tier's defects before stacking the next
idea: Effect: photoluminescence (band-edge versus defect-band emission). In monolithic 3D DRAM, after each crystalline tier forms, a wafer-scale PL scan maps trap density per subarray region; the map goes into a per-die non-volatile sparing table so defective tier regions are logically spared, and the process tool receives feedback for the next wafer.
why: 10x density: 50 tiers at 99% yield each is only 60% stack yield, which kills cost parity; PL-driven region sparing lifts effective yield above 90%, making a ~50-tier (~10x) stack cost-competitive.

title: Active negative-capacitance bitline cancels bitline load for 0.4 fF cells
idea: Effect: Miller feedback and negative impedance conversion. Each bitline pair gets a small cross-coupled negative-impedance converter, enabled only during charge sharing, that cancels ~85% of bitline capacitance; the transfer ratio Cs/(Cs+Cb) rises ~6x, so a 0.4 fF cell develops the same ~100 mV signal a 5 fF cell gives today.
why: 10x density: 0.4 fF planar caps enable a 4F^2 vertical-gate cell (1.5x) stacked 8 tiers at ~0.8x per tier (~10x). Same cost: the NIC replaces part of the sense amp, and the high-AR capacitor module is eliminated.

title: Charge-coupled circulating loops refresh by recirculation, no access transistors
idea: Effect: charge-coupled transfer. Bits are charge packets in short 64-stage CCD loops of gate-only electrodes over a buried channel (2F^2 per bit, no capacitor, no per-cell contact); packets circulate at ~2 GHz, and each lap passes a regenerator that restores packet size, so leakage and transfer inefficiency are corrected every ~30 ns. Many parallel loops give bandwidth, with ~16 ns average access.
why: 10x density: 2F^2 versus 6F^2 is 3x per layer, and 4 stacked thin-film CCD tiers give ~12x. Same cost: gates-only arrays need no capacitor module and no cell contacts.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembled arrays with defect-mapped sparing replace EUV
idea: Effect: microphase separation of high-chi block copolymers. Sub-10 nm vertical-channel cell arrays are patterned by directed self-assembly, which is cheap but leaves ~1e-4 placement defects; instead of demanding litho-perfect arrays, each mat carries ~3% spare columns plus a post-fab electrical defect map and symbol ECC, so error tolerance absorbs the disorder.
why: 10x density: F ~7 nm (versus 12 nm) at 4F^2 is ~4.4x per layer, and 2-3 tiers give ~10x. Same cost: 5-7 EUV layers (depreciation ~55% of wafer cost) are replaced by spin-coat and anneal steps.

title: Random nanowire crossbars addressed by post-fab calibrated stochastic decoder
idea: Effect: stochastic self-assembly. Sub-10 nm-pitch Si nanowire crossbars are grown or transfer-printed with gain cells at the crossings and no litho at cell scale; each wire carries a randomly doped code region, a post-fab discovery pass learns which address code activates which wire and stores a translation table, and defective wires are simply never mapped.
why: 10x density: 4F^2 crossbars at F ~5 nm without EUV give >10x bits/mm^2. Same cost: error tolerance turns disorder into a feature, so no precision patterning is paid for.

title: Rank-modulated multi-level cells immune to common-mode leakage drift
idea: Effect: correlated (common-mode) leakage drift. Groups of 8 tiny cells are written with 4 charge levels, two cells each, and information is the permutation of charges (8!/2^4 = 2520 states, ~1.4 bits/cell), not absolute levels; neighbors sharing substrate and temperature leak together, so the ranking survives long after levels drift, and a winner-take-all comparator tree reads it.
why: 10x density: ~1.4 bits/cell tolerating ~5x retention drift, on 0.5 fF cells stacked 8 tiers (~7x), gives ~10x bits/mm^2. Same cost: the comparator tree is shared per bank.

title: Band-offset Ge quantum wells store holes behind a heterobarrier
idea: Effect: heterojunction band offset. Charge is stored as holes in a buried SiGe/Ge quantum well under each access channel; the ~0.5 eV valence-band offset confines them so thermionic loss falls ~exp(-0.5 eV/kT), giving seconds of retention with no capacitor, and reads sense the threshold shift of the overlying channel (built-in gain-cell amplification).
why: 10x density: a capacitorless 1T cell at 4F^2 stacked 32 tiers by Si/SiGe superlattice epitaxy gives >10x. Same cost: the capacitor module and its EUV steps are removed.

title: Recombination-sink grid absorbs hammer electrons at much tighter pitch
idea: Effect: minority-carrier recombination in engineered short-lifetime silicon. A self-aligned buried carbon-doped or p+ grid runs between adjacent active rows; electrons injected by aggressor activation recombine inside this short-lifetime strip before reaching victim nodes, while storage junctions stay in long-lifetime silicon.
why: 10x density: tighter rows would otherwise drop hammer thresholds below ~100 and mitigation refresh would erase the gain; the sink allows ~40% row and tier pitch shrink, which with 16-tier stacking gives ~10x at the cost of one implant or epi step.

title: Electret field plates in isolation trenches defuse GIDL hot spots
idea: Effect: electret fixed charge. A permanently charged dielectric (Al2O3 with ~1e13 q/cm^2 of fixed negative charge, or implant-charged SiO2) lines the isolation trench beside each storage junction, counter-biasing the junction edge where band-to-band tunneling GIDL peaks; this cuts the peak field ~30% and tail leakage ~10x with no wiring.
why: 10x density: shrinking pitch 3x raises junction fields and blows up tails; passive electret field shaping keeps 64 ms retention for 0.5 fF caps in densely stacked lateral cells (~10x) at the cost of one liner deposition.

title: NEMS relay access switches give zero-leakage tiny storage nodes
idea: Effect: electrostatic actuation of nano-electromechanical relays. The access transistor becomes an electrostatically actuated beam with a ~10 nm gap, and the air gap in the off state means no subthreshold or junction leakage, so a 0.1 fF parasitic node holds data far beyond 64 ms; the relays are metal-only and low-temperature, so they stack in BEOL.
why: 10x density: about 10 BEOL layers of 4F^2 crosspoint relays over CMOS periphery give ~10x. Same cost: metal deposition and no EUV. The reliability risk is contact wear against DRAM-level endurance (~1e15 cycles).

title: Oxygen-vacancy back gate trims every leaky row after test
idea: Effect: field-driven oxygen-vacancy drift in HfOx. Each stacked thin-film tier has a back-gate dielectric of oxygen-deficient HfOx; after retention test, a forming-like pulse drifts vacancies toward or away from the channel, permanently shifting a tail row's Vt by ~+100 mV: a non-volatile per-row analog leakage fuse.
why: 10x density: cheap thin-film tiers have broad Vt spreads, and per-row trim collapses the tail so low-cost channels meet retention in 32-tier stacks (~10x). Same cost: the back gate is one extra deposition per tier.

title: Band-to-band tunnel-FET access device gives attoamp-class off state
idea: Effect: interband (Zener) tunneling as the switching mechanism. A gated p-i-n tunnel FET replaces the access MOSFET; with no band overlap in the off state, leakage is limited by a reverse-biased junction (~1e-18 A, ~1000x below MOSFET tails), while its uA-class on-current still charges a 0.3 fF node in ~5 ns. The unidirectional conduction is handled by a split read/write gate design.
why: 10x density: 0.3 fF instead of 5 fF removes the capacitor module; a vertical TFET at 4F^2 stacked 6-8 tiers gives ~10x at similar cost.

title: Z-channel codes exploit leakage that only drains ones
idea: Effect: thermodynamic relaxation asymmetry, where leakage only moves a cell toward equilibrium. Data is mapped per subarray (true/anti-cell aware) so the charged state is always logical 1, making retention errors strictly 1->0; asymmetric-error codes (Varshamov-Tenengolts, Z-channel LDPC) then correct t errors with ~half the parity of symmetric codes, and write-side sparse coding (<=40% ones) shrinks the vulnerable population.
why: 10x density: ~100x more raw retention BER tolerated at the same ~8% parity lets poor-retention 0.3 fF thin-film cells stack 24 tiers (~10x) at the same cost.

title: Megasonic in-package anneal heals interface traps in cheap poly channels
idea: Effect: acoustically stimulated defect reconfiguration (ultrasound-induced interface-trap reduction in MOS structures). A transducer in the module periodically injects MHz acoustic energy into the 3D die, reordering and passivating traps in low-cost polysilicon thin-film access transistors and narrowing their leakage tail in the field (self-healing).
why: 10x density: poly-Si tiers cost far less per layer than single-crystal but have ~100x worse tails; healing them makes 40-tier poly-Si 3D DRAM (~10x) viable at the same cost.

title: Dithered multi-comparator sensing reads four-level cells reliably
idea: Effect: stochastic resonance and dithering. After charge sharing the bitline voltage holds for a few ns; three coarse comparators shared per 8 bitlines sample it several times with injected calibrated dither, and averaging resolves below comparator offset, reading 4 levels (2 bits) from a ~0.8 fF cell before a DAC-driven restore.
why: 10x density: 2 bits/cell times a 12-tier stack of ~0.8 fF cells (~5x) gives ~10x bits/mm^2. Same cost: comparators and DACs are amortized across 8 bitlines, with no capacitor module.

title: Significance-aware placement puts AI mantissa bits in tail-prone rows
idea: Effect: trap-assisted-tunneling retention tails are lognormal and concentrated in identifiable rows. The controller profiles row retention and packs low-significance bits (FP8/BF16 mantissa LSBs, KV-cache low bits) into tail-prone rows refreshed 8x less often and without ECC, while sign and exponent bits go to strong rows with ECC.
why: 10x density: a ~10x-dense 3D die where only ~30% of rows meet strict retention is still fully sold, with the rest used as 'approximate bits' for AI tensors that tolerate ~1e-4 BER with <0.1% accuracy loss, raising effective density at the same cost.
